body:
One use case illustrating the issue: 

Initial: Configure props is `hitsPerPage=3`

Step1: pass new props to configure to be `hitsPerPage=1`

Now the `search state` has `hitsPerPage=1`. 

Step2: pass new props to configure to be `hitsPerPage=2`

If we look at the search state first, this will never be applied. 

-- 

One obvious use case to read from the `search state` would be when you are loading the page and read the state from the URL. So reading from the state when the component did mount should do the trick for this case, but for now we don't have the architecture for it. 

Before the PR, the way it could have worked was when unmounting systematically the `<Configure/>` widget before passing it new props. 

With the PR, the search state is never taken into account, and you need to pass the right props directly to the `<Configure/>` widget.
